ak_falcon_rock.blurb: Falcon Rock is one of the larger outcrops within the East Grapefruit group, sitting on a low dome beside the Elliott Highway north of Fairbanks. Eleven climbs are spread over a few distinct faces: five top-rope lines, three bolted sport routes and three gear routes. Most grades fall between 5.7 and 5.9, with a small cluster of 5.11 test pieces. The limestone is mostly short, though the west-facing Hole in the Wall face holds the longer lines. A friendly stop for mixed-ability groups and newer leaders who want an easy walk and a range of grades.

ak_tunnel_vision_wall.blurb: Tunnel Vision Wall is a small, gear-only crag in the Fairangel Gap above the Hatcher Pass road, at roughly 3,500 feet. All eleven routes are trad, with grades running from 5.7 up to 5.11 and the bulk of them in the 5.8 to 5.9 range. The face leans just past vertical and is cut into two halves by a finger crack on its right side, so expect crack and edge climbing rather than slabs. Short routes and a brief walk from the road make it a quick half-day objective.
ak_tunnel_vision_wall.parking_note: Leave the car by the outhouse near the start of the valley, then follow the path on the road side of the creek up toward the gap.

ak_kiliak_wall.blurb: Kiliak Wall is a south-facing cliff in the Eagle River valley outside Anchorage, reached by a long uphill walk rather than a roadside pullout. Ten of its eleven climbs are bolted and one is a gear route. Grades center on 5.10, with a few easier lines around 5.8 and several at 5.11. Because the face catches sun through most of the day it dries quickly and suits spring and fall outings. Views over the valley are a big part of the appeal, but hold quality varies, so test holds near the tops of lines.

ak_crescent_moon.blurb: Crescent Moon is a single beach boulder of rust-colored rock with a moon-shaped mark, on the shore of Captain Cook State Recreation Area on the Kenai Peninsula. It carries eleven problems, with about half at V0 to V2 and the rest stretching up to roughly V6, so beginners and strong boulderers both get something. The block is tall for a beach boulder and is well exposed only when the tide is out, so plan around the tide table. The setting is quiet, with mostly anglers and beachcombers nearby.
ak_crescent_moon.parking_note: Use the day-use lot at the end of the road in the state recreation area, then go down to the beach and walk along the sand.

ak_mosquito_ledge.blurb: Mosquito Ledge is a long cliff along the Seward Highway south of Anchorage, regarded as one of the better crags on that corridor. Of its eleven routes, eight are sport and three are trad, graded from 5.8 through the 5.11 range, with the bulk split evenly between 5.10 and 5.11. Lines are long for the region and the rock is sound by local standards, though moss and forest growth creep in where traffic is light. The cliff stands well back from the road, so it feels remote, and bug spray is worthwhile in summer.

ak_royal_tower_the.blurb: The Royal Tower is an 8,130-foot granite summit in the Little Switzerland group of the Alaska Range, roughly 50 miles northwest of Talkeetna. It rises more than 2,600 feet above the Pika Glacier, and its faces and central couloir hold committing alpine lines. Of eleven routes, most are rock climbs from 5.8 to 5.11, with one ice route and one mixed line around M4. Expect a full expedition-style objective: glacier travel, long days and rappel descents, best attempted by experienced parties.
